{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,z)\,r\,dz\,dr\,d\theta .
$$

If $(r,\theta ,z)$ are the cylindrical polar coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the formulas

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,z=z.
$$

First, let's sketch the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane:

![](images/cc/ccc5cab37aed89c0d701ce0195414796211ddc73a498eaaa1ff145a45c42e9fd.png)

The region $R$ is one-half of a right vertical cylinder of radius $3$ whose axis passes through the point $(3,0)$ in the $xy$-plane, and is

- bounded below by $z=y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,$ and

- bounded above by $z=6.$

With that in mind, let's now write the $(x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2}=9$ in polar coordinates:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2}+{y}^{2} & =9 \\ (r\operatorname{cos}\theta -3)^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}\theta )^{2} & =3 \\ {r}^{2}{\operatorname{cos}}^{2}\theta -6r\operatorname{cos}\theta +9+{r}^{2}{\operatorname{sin}}^{2}\theta  & =9 \\ {r}^{2}({\operatorname{cos}}^{2}\theta +{\operatorname{sin}}^{2}\theta )-6r\operatorname{cos}\theta  & =0 \\ {r}^{2}-6r\operatorname{cos}\theta  & =0 \\ r(r-6\operatorname{cos}\theta ) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Since $r$ cannot be identical to zero on the entire semicircle, we must have $r=6\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .$

As a result, in cylindrical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
\mathrm{Δ}=\{(r,\theta ,z)\hspace{0.167em}:\hspace{0.167em}0\le r\le 6\operatorname{cos}\theta ,\hspace{0.222em}\frac{3\pi }{2}\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\hspace{0.222em}r\operatorname{sin}\theta \le z\le 6\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{z+1}}\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}V & ={∭}_{\mathrm{Δ}}\frac{1}{\sqrt{z+1}}\cdot r\hspace{0.222em}\mathrm{d}z\hspace{0.167em}\mathrm{d}r\hspace{0.167em}\mathrm{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{{\color{blue}6\operatorname{cos}\theta }}}{\int }_{\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{{\color{blue}r\operatorname{sin}\theta }}}^{6}\bbox[Gainsboro, 2pt]{{\color{blue}\frac{r}{\sqrt{z+1}}}}\hspace{0.222em}\mathrm{d}z\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}r\hspace{0.222em}\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$"]]
